name: EndoVis 2020 (Endoscopic Vision Challenge, MICCAI 2020 umbrella record)
trajectory_unit: Umbrella challenge-design record with no data of its own. It describes four sub-challenge datasets: CATARACTS workflow (one video = one cataract surgery), CATARACTS semantic segmentation (annotated frames from CATARACTS videos), MISAW (one case = one robotic micro-anastomosis training trial) and SurgVisDom (VR / porcine task video clips). These are audited separately as DS114 (CATARACTS), DS143 (MISAW) and DS170 (SurgVisDom). Verdicts below summarise the sub-challenge descriptions in this record and name the sub-challenge each refers to.
n_trajectories_quote: 50 cataract surgeries have been recorded. [...] Training: 17 cases [...] Testing: 10 cases [...] 22 (VR) + 3 (porcine) training cases will be made available for the 3 tasks resulting in a total set of 75 training videos. The test set will contain a total of 30 video clips

D1.quote: Each frame of the videos has a list of twenty classes, indicating in which activities the surgeon is at. [...] Kinematic data (x, y, z, alpha, beta, gamma at 30hz)
D1.reason: Time-stamped human action variables exist in sub-challenges (CATARACTS per-frame surgeon activities; MISAW robot kinematics + per-timestamp activities; SurgVisDom per-clip activity labels), but no sub-challenge reaches 200 human trajectories (CATARACTS 50, MISAW 27, SurgVisDom <=105 clips). No single release unit exists for the umbrella record.

D2.quote: Workflow annotation (not provide for test cases), containing for each timestamp the label for phase, steps, [...] Each video clip will include a label of the activity being performed.
D2.reason: The annotation inventories described for all four sub-challenges are activity/phase/step labels and segmentation masks; no outcome (task success, skill score, error, complication, post-action sensor measurement) is documented.

D3.quote: Training, validation and test cases are videos of cataract surgery. [...] Video and kinematic data are recorded synchronously at 30 Hz.
D3.reason: PASS only for the CATARACTS-workflow (full surgery videos) and MISAW (synchronous 30 Hz trials) sub-datasets. CATARACTS-segmentation is annotated frames and SurgVisDom is video clips (both would FAIL).

D4.quote: Surgeries were performed by three surgeons: a renowned expert, a one-year experienced surgeon and an intern. [...] Brest University Hospital, France. [...] Surgeries were performed under an OPMI Lumera T microscope (Carl Zeiss Meditec, Jena, Germany).
D4.reason: CATARACTS: one site, one microscope; 50 videos by 3 surgeons, but the per-video surgeon assignment is not given in this record (see DS114). MISAW: per-case operator counts are given and all are <20 (FAIL). SurgVisDom: no per-trajectory factor. No factor is shown to have >=2 levels with >=20 trajectories.

D5.quote: CC BY NC SA. [...] Publicly available for non-commercial use after the challenge and the challenge paper submission. [...] CC BY NC ND.
D5.reason: CATARACTS and MISAW data: CC BY-NC-SA (research use; derived material shareable under the same terms); CATARACTS also requires a signed terms-and-conditions document at registration. SurgVisDom: CC BY-NC-ND, which does not allow sharing adapted material (FAIL for that sub-challenge). The Zenodo record licence (cc-by-nd-4.0) covers the design document only.

D6.quote: This is the challenge design document for the "Endoscopic Vision Challenge", accepted for MICCAI 2020.
D6.reason: The record holds only a 9.1 MB design PDF. No dataset sizes are documented for any sub-challenge.

D7.quote: Each frame of the videos has a list of twenty classes, indicating in which activities the surgeon is at. [...] Frames from 35 cataract surgery videos have been annotated for scene segmentation.
D7.reason: Per-frame human activity labels (CATARACTS) and per-timestamp phase/step labels (MISAW) vary within trajectories and are not acquisition metadata.

D8.reason: No acquisition factor meets D4 in this record (CATARACTS operator assignment undocumented here; MISAW operators <20 each; single sites/devices).

counts.collection_mode: All human: CATARACTS clinician-performed cataract surgery (50); MISAW human teleoperation of a master-slave robot on a training task by 3 expert surgeons + 3 engineering students (27); SurgVisDom VR (da Vinci SimNow) and porcine tasks by surgeons/non-surgeons (75 training videos + 30 test clips).
counts.site: CATARACTS: Brest University Hospital (1). MISAW: University of Tokyo (1). SurgVisDom: Intuitive Surgical training labs.
counts.device: CATARACTS: Zeiss OPMI Lumera T microscope. MISAW: master-slave robotic platform + HD stereo-microscope. SurgVisDom: da Vinci (SimNow VR + porcine).
counts.operator: CATARACTS: 3 surgeons (per-video assignment not given). MISAW train: Surgeon 2: 3, Surgeon 3: 4, Engineering student 1: 6, Engineering student 2: 4; test: Surgeon 1: 4, Engineering student 3: 6.
counts.annotation_type: CATARACTS: per-frame 20 surgical activities. CATARACTS-seg: pixel segmentation of frames from 35 videos. MISAW: per-timestamp phase/step/left-hand/right-hand activity at 30 Hz + kinematics. SurgVisDom: per-clip task label.

notes: Umbrella record. The sub-challenge datasets are separate entries: DS114 CATARACTS, DS143 MISAW, DS170 SurgVisDom. Even counted together, the distinct trajectories (<=50+27+105=182) are below 200, and they are not one release unit. Not SS-eligible and not RA-eligible.

name: ESAD / SARAS-ESAD / SARAS-MESAD
trajectory_unit: One complete robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) recording: real patient (ESAD = MESAD-Real) or phantom (MESAD-Phantom). Released as JPEG frame sequences with per-frame label files.
n_trajectories_quote: the first dataset (MESAD-Real) is composed by 4 annotated videos of real surgeries on human patients, while the second dataset (MESAD-Phantom) contains 5 annotated videos of surgical procedures on artificial human anatomies.

D1.quote: Given a video frame, we draw bounding box around surgical tool which is performing action and label it with action label. [...] we collected four complete prostatectomy procedure with the consent of the patients and hospital.
D1.source: https://zenodo.org/records/4471476 (ESAD paper PDF; arXiv:2006.07164; local copy /media/user/LaCie/medvideo_gate/DS129/ESAD_paper.pdf) ; https://zenodo.org/api/records/4471476
D1.reason: Frame-level human-annotated surgeon action labels (21 classes at 1 fps) are a time-stamped action variable, but there are only 4 real and 5 phantom procedures, far below 200. Collection mode: clinician-performed (real) and phantom training procedures; no programmatic collection.

D2.quote: Each instance is annotated with a bounding box and its action label from classes.
D2.source: https://zenodo.org/records/4471476 (ESAD paper PDF; arXiv:2006.07164; local copy /media/user/LaCie/medvideo_gate/DS129/ESAD_paper.pdf)
D2.reason: The only annotation is action bounding boxes with action class. No outcome variable is documented.

D3.quote: Each directory has frames names in the order of their occurrence (e.g. RARP2_frame_1.jpg, RARP2_frame_2.jpg, etc). [...] Each video is recorded videos at 30 FPS but annotation are performed at 1 FPS
D3.source: https://saras-esad.grand-challenge.org/download/ ; https://zenodo.org/records/4471476 (ESAD paper PDF; arXiv:2006.07164; local copy /media/user/LaCie/medvideo_gate/DS129/ESAD_paper.pdf)
D3.reason: Frames come from complete procedures and are ordered, but the release is image frames, not video. The sampling rate and contiguity of the released frames are not stated (annotation at 1 fps; "Not all the frames in the dataset are labeled"). MESAD describes its data as "a set of video frames annotated for static action detection purposes".

D4.quote: Dataset contains digital recordings from da Vinci Xi robotic system [...] Dataset is created from the four sessions of complete prostatectomy procedure performed by expert surgeons on real patients.
D4.reason: One robotic system and 4 real (+5 phantom) procedures. No per-trajectory site/device/operator table, and too few trajectories for 2 levels with >=20.

D5.quote: License: This dataset is released under CC BY-NC-SA license. [...] This dataset is licensed by a CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license.
D5.reason: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 permits non-commercial research use and sharing of adapted material (derived features) under the same terms. The challenge rules add "Participating teams are not allowed to share the challenge data."

D6.quote: Training data contains a total of 22,601 annotated frames and contains 28,055 action instances.
D6.reason: Frame counts are given, but no file size is documented.

D7.quote: Each frame can have multiple number of action instances. Each instance is annotated with a bounding box and its action label from classes.
D7.source: https://zenodo.org/records/4471476 (ESAD paper PDF; arXiv:2006.07164; local copy /media/user/LaCie/medvideo_gate/DS129/ESAD_paper.pdf)
D7.reason: Frame-level human annotations (action class + box around tool and organ, verified by a medical professional) vary within trajectories and are not acquisition metadata.

counts.collection_mode: Clinician-performed RARP on patients (4; da Vinci Xi) + procedures on artificial phantoms (5).
counts.site: Not documented per video. Single SARAS clinical source implied; the paper affiliation lists San Raffaele Hospital, Milan.
counts.device: da Vinci Xi, 8 mm binocular endoscope, 0 or 30 degree lens (monocular stream used).
counts.annotation_type: Bounding boxes + action class (21 real / 14 phantom classes, 11 shared). ESAD: train 22,601 / val 4,574 / test 6,223 frames. MESAD: Real train 23,366 / val 2,024 images; Phantom train 22,609 / val 2,285 images.

notes: Grand-Challenge pages: "Once you are registered with this challenge, you can download the training and validation dataset". Not SS- or RA-eligible (9 trajectories).

name: Fetoscopy Placenta Dataset (Bano et al. MICCAI 2020)
trajectory_unit: One in-vivo TTTS fetoscopic procedure video. Only sub-sampled annotated frames and short unannotated clips are released.
n_trajectories_quote: In total, there are 483 annotated placental images from 6 in invivo video, where the videos are named as video01, video02,..., video006.

D1.quote: The folder contains the images and manually annotated ground-truth vessel segmentation masks for a sub-sampled set of images from 6 different fetoscopic videos.
D1.reason: No action variable is recorded. 6 videos.

D2.quote: These video clips contain sequential frames which are not manually annotated for placental vessel but the predicted maps returned from the leave-one-video-out cross-validation as reported in \cite{bano2019vessel} are provided for vessel registration and mosaicking.
D2.reason: No outcome variable. The clip maps are model-derived, which never qualifies.

D3.quote: a sub-sampled set of images from 6 different fetoscopic videos [...] The folder contains video clips from the 6 fetoscopic videos.
D3.reason: Sub-sampled frames plus short clips (50-400 frames each). No continuous full procedure recordings.

D4.quote: video01 - 121 images
D4.reason: Only 6 videos. No per-video site/device/operator is documented.

D5.quote: The Fetoscopy Placenta Dataset is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).
D5.reason: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: non-commercial research use; adapted material shareable under the same terms.

D6.quote: "name": "Vessel_registration_unannotated_clips.zip", "size": 280035372
D6.reason: Repository file sizes: 3,042 + 189,124,327 + 280,035,372 bytes = 0.47 GB total, far below 2.02 TB.

D7.quote: manually annotated ground-truth vessel segmentation masks
D7.reason: Manual vessel masks on 483 frames vary within videos (scene content). The clip maps are model-derived and do not qualify.

counts.collection_mode: Clinician-performed TTTS fetoscopic laser procedures (in vivo).
counts.device: Not documented.
counts.annotation_type: Manual vessel segmentation on 483 frames (video01 121, video02 101, video03 39, video04 88, video05 37, video06 97); 6 unannotated clips (950 frames) with model-predicted maps.

notes: Superseded in scale by FetReg (DS131). Not eligible for either arm.

n_trajectories_quote: from 18 in-vivo TTTS fetoscopy procedures and 18 short video clips of an average length of 411 frames [...] an unseen test dataset of 658 pixel-annotated images from 6 fetoscopic procedures and 6 short clips.

D1.quote: we released a dataset of 2060 images, pixel-annotated for vessels, tool, fetus and background classes

D2.quote: No registration annotations were provided as it is not possible
D2.reason: No outcome variable is documented (pixel segmentation; unannotated registration clips).

D3.quote: 18 short video clips of an average length of 411 frames

D4.quote: For each video, center ID (I - UCLH, II - IGG), image resolution,

Leuven), but Table 2 lists only I and II. Device ("varying facilities (e.g., device, light scope)") is not per video; operator is not documented.

D5.quote: The FetReg2021 challenge data (both training and test) is now publicly available [...] under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license.

name: Hashemi 2025 human robotic surgery dataset (Closing the data gap)
sources_consulted: https://www.synapse.org/#!Synapse:syn65669574 (wiki + anonymous file listing via Synapse REST API)
trajectory_unit: One clinical robot-assisted procedure recording. 27 video files on Synapse, since some procedures are split into parts or sub-clips by surgeon.
n_trajectories_quote: The clinical data consisted of 15 full surgical procedure recordings made on urological, general surgical and thoracic procedures

D1.quote: all videos were labelled temporally according to whether suturing or dissection sequences occurred for the action recognition task
D1.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12641048/ (Hashemi et al., J Robot Surg 2025, doi:10.1007/s11701-025-02994-y)
D1.reason: Human-annotated time-stamped action labels (suturing/dissection, suture type, needle driving/handling) from clinician-performed procedures, but only 15 procedures (<200).

D2.quote: For skills assessment, complete videos were labelled as either ‘experienced’ or ‘novice’ depending on whether the procedure was done by an experienced or a novice RAS surgeon
D2.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12641048/ (Hashemi et al., J Robot Surg 2025, doi:10.1007/s11701-025-02994-y)
D2.reason: The "skill" label is operator experience category (operator metadata defined by case volume), not an outcome after the action. No other outcome is documented.

D3.quote: The clinical data consisted of 15 full surgical procedure recordings
D3.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12641048/ (Hashemi et al., J Robot Surg 2025, doi:10.1007/s11701-025-02994-y)
D3.reason: Full procedure recordings (some split into parts by surgeon).

D4.quote: The study was conducted at Departments of Urology, Gastro-intestinal surgery, and Thoracic surgery at Aalborg University Hospital, Aalborg, Denmark. [...] We included 12 surgeons, eight experienced RAS surgeons and four novice RAS surgeons
D4.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12641048/ (Hashemi et al., J Robot Surg 2025, doi:10.1007/s11701-025-02994-y)
D4.reason: One site, one platform (da Vinci), 12 surgeons over 15 procedures. No level reaches 20.

D5.quote: The data and codes are open-source. However, when using it, please make a reference to our paper and repository.
D5.reason: Described as "open-source" but no licence is named. Derived-feature release is not addressed.

D6.quote: Download the video data from the 'Videos'-folder.
D6.reason: Synapse listing: Videos folder 61,044,807,121 bytes (27 mp4) + Labels 335,456 bytes + root files 372,783,137 bytes, about 61.4 GB.

D7.quote: All actions were labeled from start to completion.
D7.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12641048/ (Hashemi et al., J Robot Surg 2025, doi:10.1007/s11701-025-02994-y)
D7.reason: Temporal human labels of suturing/dissection segments vary within procedures (single annotator).

counts.collection_mode: Clinician-performed robot-assisted surgery on patients (some procedures shared between surgeons).
counts.device: da Vinci Surgical System recorded via HDMI capture cards (15 fps, 2560x720).
counts.operator: 12 surgeons (8 experienced, 4 novice); per-procedure distribution in the paper Supplementary Table 5 (not inspected).
counts.annotation_type: BORIS temporal labels: suturing (single/running; needle driving/handling) vs dissection; video-level experienced/novice label; 27 per-video xlsx label files.

notes: Synapse file download needs a Synapse account (anonymous file request returned HTTP 403). No data-use agreement is documented. Not eligible.

name: HeiChole (EndoVis 2019 Surgical Workflow and Skill) / HeiSurF
trajectory_unit: One laparoscopic cholecystectomy video (camera insertion to last removal).
n_trajectories_quote: The data set contains n=33 videos of laparoscopic cholecystectomies from three surgical centers in Germany with a total video length of 22 hours.

D1.quote: Annotations for action were a 4D binary vector per frame indicating if the corresponding action is being performed (1) or not (0)).
D1.reason: Framewise human action labels (grasp/hold/cut/clip, with performer) in clinician-performed surgery, but only 33 videos (24 training videos are public on Synapse). This is below 200.

D2.quote: To assess the surgical skill, the videos were scored using the modified Global Operative Assessment of Laparoscopic Skills (GOALS).
D2.reason: Candidate outcome: human-rated modified GOALS skill (5 dimensions, 1-5) per full video and per phase video (Calot triangle dissection, gallbladder dissection), rated by two medical students. This is a trajectory-level rating, not a post-action time point.

D3.quote: Every video starts at the first insertion of the laparoscopic camera into the patient’s abdomen and ends with the last removal of the laparoscopic camera.
D3.reason: Full continuous procedure videos. Extra-abdominal frames are censored to white frames.

D4.quote: The operation videos at Heidelberg University Hospital (n=15) were recorded with a laparoscopic 2D camera (Karl Storz SE & Co KG, Tuttlingen Germany) [...] The operation videos at Salem Hospital (n=15) and the GRN-hospital Sinsheim (n=3) were recorded with the laparoscopic 2D camera ENDOCAM Logic HD (Richard Wolf GmbH, Knittlingen, Germany)
D4.reason: Site levels 15/15/3 and device levels 15 (Storz) / 18 (Wolf) are all <20. Only dataset-level counts are given; no per-video site table was found publicly. Operator is not documented.

D5.quote: ShareAlike (CC BY-NC-SA) license on Synapse (https://www.synapse.org/#!Synapse:syn18824884/files/), which means that it will be publicly available for non-commercial usage.
D5.reason: CC BY-NC-SA: non-commercial research use; adapted material shareable under the same terms. Synapse registration with agreement to cite.

D6.quote: For each surgery, the video captured by the endoscope is provided.
D6.reason: Synapse listing: Videos/Full 66.4 GB + Videos/Full/HD 115.8 GB + Videos/Skill 45.3 GB + annotations about 0.7 GB, about 228.2 GB total.

D7.quote: Annotations for surgical phase were one value per frame.
D7.reason: Per-frame human phase and instrument-presence labels vary within trajectories.

counts.site: Heidelberg University Hospital 15, Salem Hospital 15, GRN-hospital Sinsheim 3 (dataset-level). Training split: 12 Heidelberg + 12 Salem; test 3/3/3.
counts.device: Karl Storz 2D camera (Heidelberg, 15); Richard Wolf ENDOCAM Logic HD (Salem + Sinsheim, 18).
counts.annotation_type: Framewise phase (7), action (4, with performer), instrument category/type presence; modified GOALS skill (5 dimensions) per full/Calot/dissection video.

notes: Synapse listing shows 24 public full videos (Hei-Chole1..24) with annotation folders Action/Instrument/Phase/Skill. RA candidate on D2/D3/D5/D6 but fails D1 (n<200) and D4. One HeiChole video (HeiChole2) is reused in PhaKIR (DS147).

name: HeiCo (Heidelberg Colorectal Data Set)
sources_consulted: https://www.synapse.org/#!Synapse:syn21903917 (wiki + anonymous file listing incl. all 10,040 frame folders)
trajectory_unit: One laparoscopic colorectal procedure (video + device CSV + phase CSV per procedure folder).
n_trajectories_quote: Our data set comprises 30 laparoscopic videos and corresponding sensor data from medical devices in the operating room for three different types of laparoscopic surgery.

D1.quote: Annotations include surgical phase information and information on the status of medical devices for all frames
D1.reason: Per-frame device-status streams and expert phase labels exist, but there are only 30 procedures (<200). Clinician-performed; no programmatic collection.

D2.quote: KARL STORZ OR1 FUSION® was used to record additional data streams from medical devices in the room, namely Insufflator Thermoflator, OR lights, cold light fountain Xenon 300, and Camera Image 1.
D2.reason: Candidate: OR device sensor streams (e.g. insufflator), recorded independently of the video. The parameter list (Table 1) could not be rendered, so it is not verified whether any stream is a post-action measurement rather than a device setting.

D3.quote: frames corresponding to parts of the surgery performed outside of the abdomen were manually identified and subsequently replaced by blue images.
D3.reason: Full procedure videos; extra-abdominal frames replaced, not cut.

D4.quote: Furthermore, we acquired data from only one hospital. This implies limited variability with respect to the acquisition conditions as only one specific endoscope and light source were used.
D4.reason: Single site and device; 30 procedures; operator not documented.

D5.quote: The data set was published under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike (CC BY-NC-SA) license, which means that it will be publicly available for non-commercial usage.
D5.reason: CC BY-NC-SA: non-commercial research use; derived material shareable under the same terms.

D6.quote: The complete data set contains 10,040 image frames.
D6.reason: Synapse listing: procedure-level files (.avi + Device.csv + Phase.csv) 161.2 GB; all 10,040 instrument-segmentation frame folders (raw.png, 10s_video.zip, masks) 870.1 GB; total about 1.03 TB, under 2.02 TB. The videos-only subset is 161 GB.

D7.quote: Annotations include surgical phase labels for all frames in the videos as well as instance-wise segmentation masks for surgical instruments in more than 10,000 individual frames.
D7.reason: Per-frame human phase labels and instrument masks vary within trajectories.

counts.device: 1 (KARL STORZ Image 1 camera, 30 degree telescope, Xenon 300; OR1 FUSION).
counts.annotation_type: Per-frame phase (single expert surgeon), per-frame device status, instrument instance masks on 10,040 frames (8,228 masks).

notes: The download script states "1. Create an account for synapse 2. Register for the Challenge". The 30 HeiCo videos are reused in ORena FOCUS (DS145, HeiCo-FOCUS). Not eligible (n=30).

name: HiSWA-RLLS (EndoVis 2024 Hierarchical Surgical Workflow Analysis, Robotic Left Lateral Sectionectomy)
trajectory_unit: One robotic left lateral sectionectomy video (execution phase, without access/closure). Released on Synapse as per-video image archives plus per-video 5-fps annotation JSON.
n_trajectories_quote: From December 2016 to May 2019, 45 cases of RLLS videos were enrolled in our dataset.

D1.quote: Frames of RLLS videos were annotated with step, task, and activity based on prior studies [...] The temporal annotations in this study were made by three senior surgeons with more than 5 years of clinical experience.
D1.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10583914/ (Liu et al., Int J Surg 2023, doi:10.1097/JS9.0000000000000559)
D1.reason: Per-frame human activity labels (instrument-action-target) in clinician-performed robotic surgery, but only 45 cases (about 30-31 videos in the public Synapse listing). This is below 200.

D2.quote: The authors defined those activities that truly contribute to the surgery as effective frames, while other activities are labeled as under-effective frames.
D2.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10583914/ (Liu et al., Int J Surg 2023, doi:10.1097/JS9.0000000000000559)
D2.reason: The documented annotations are step/task/activity plus an under-effective flag. No outcome after the action is documented.

D3.quote: All frames of RLLS videos in this study are labeled with temporal annotations. [...] we sample the videos into frames with a fixed 5fps sampling rate
D3.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10583914/ (Liu et al., Int J Surg 2023, doi:10.1097/JS9.0000000000000559)
D3.reason: Continuous execution-phase recordings, released as image sequences with per-video "_fps5" annotation files (Synapse). Caveat: released as extracted frames ("surgical images extracted from clinical procedures"), not native video; access/closure phases excluded.

D4.quote: All operations were performed by four expert surgeons who had finished at least 20 RLLS previously using the da Vinci Si Surgical System (Intuitive Surgical). [...] we use experts B and C for training and experts A and D for testing, which is in a 34:11 split. [...] the cases included in this study were acquired from a single center
D4.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10583914/ (Liu et al., Int J Surg 2023, doi:10.1097/JS9.0000000000000559)
D4.reason: One centre and one robot. 4 surgeons: B+C together 34 and A+D 11, so at most one surgeon can have >=20. Per-video surgeon is not documented publicly (the Synapse prefixes A/B/C are undocumented).

D5.quote: Access to the data of the challenge will only be provided once the following form has been filled out, scanned, and sent to ShangZhao
D5.reason: No data licence is stated. Access is via a signed form and the EndoVis rules. The CC BY-SA 4.0 of the journal article covers the article only.

D6.quote: ALL annotation files are released !!!
D6.reason: Synapse listing: Images folder 70,803,479,656 bytes (31 zip) + Annotations 43,142,456 bytes (30 JSON), about 70.8 GB.

D7.quote: Effective frames of all RLLS videos are annotated with three hierarchical levels of 4 steps, 12 tasks, and 26 activities.
D7.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10583914/ (Liu et al., Int J Surg 2023, doi:10.1097/JS9.0000000000000559)
D7.reason: Per-frame human workflow labels vary within trajectories.

counts.device: 1 (da Vinci Si; Hisense surgical record system, 60 fps, 1280x1024).
counts.operator: 4 expert surgeons A-D (B+C: 34 cases, A+D: 11); per-video assignment not public.
counts.annotation_type: Per-frame step (4) / task (12) / activity (26) + under-effective flag, by 3 senior surgeons; public Synapse annotation files A00-A04, B00-B13, C00-C10 (_fps5.json).

notes: The test split is non-public ("quantified using a non-public test split of the publicly available HiSWA-RLLS dataset"). Not eligible.

name: iMED: A Multi-Endoscope Dataset for Surgical 3D Perception
trajectory_unit: Ambiguous under the gate unit. The data are 340 short synchronized multi-endoscope sequences (scripted camera-motion / manipulation episodes), recorded in sessions on 14 specimens (ex vivo, postmortem, live). Counted conservatively per specimen session (sequences of one session = clips of one "procedure"): 14. If each sequence were a trajectory: 340, but only a v1.0 subset (about one scene per session) is public.
n_trajectories_quote: 340 sequences (~170K synchronized timepoints, 4 views per timepoint) recorded simultaneously from two physically independent stereo endoscopes across ex vivo, postmortem, and live surgical settings spanning 14 specimens

D1.quote: movement_types=["off_camera_manipulation", "tool_manipulation"],
D1.reason: No time-stamped human action variable is documented. Sequences carry a per-sequence motion category (e.g. circular/zoom/lateral camera motion, tool_manipulation), i.e. scripted experimental conditions, and the operator/collection mode is not documented. name: PhaKIR (Surgical Procedure Phase, Keypoint, and Instrument Recognition)
trajectory_unit: One complete laparoscopic cholecystectomy video.
n_trajectories_quote: We present the Surgical Procedure Phase, Keypoint, and Instrument Recognition (PhaKIR) dataset, comprising eight complete laparoscopic cholecystectomy videos recorded at three medical centers.

D1.quote: The dataset provides frame-level annotations for three interconnected tasks: surgical phase recognition (485,875 frames), instrument keypoint estimation (19,435 frames), and instrument instance segmentation (19,435 frames).
D1.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.06549 (Rueckert et al.; Data in Brief 68:113147, 2026)
D1.reason: No action variable (phases, keypoints, masks); 8 videos.

D2.quote: Finally, the dataset contains only RGB video; no other multimodal information is included.
D2.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.06549 (Rueckert et al.; Data in Brief 68:113147, 2026)
D2.reason: No outcome.

D3.quote: For surgical phase recognition, every frame was annotated (25 fps), resulting in 485,875 labeled frames.
D3.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.06549 (Rueckert et al.; Data in Brief 68:113147, 2026)
D3.reason: Complete procedure videos at 25 fps (extra-abdominal sequences removed, with cut indices provided).
